title: Work and Energy
seo_title: Work and Energy Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 10)
standard_text: Work, Energy and Power: Work done by a Force, Energy, power; Kinetic and Potential energy; Law of conservation of energy (excluding commercial unit of Energy).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 10: work done by a force, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy and power. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: W = F × s; KE = ½mv²; PE = mgh.
key_sub: Energy changes form but is never created or destroyed.
body_html:
How to think about it

Work is done when a force moves an object in its direction: W = F × s, in joules. If there is no displacement, or the force is at right angles to it, no work is done; a force against the motion does negative work.

Kinetic energy is ½mv² and gravitational potential energy is mgh. As a ball falls, its PE changes into KE while the total stays the same. Power is the rate of doing work, P = W ÷ t, in watts (1 W = 1 J/s).

Example

KE of 5 kg at 4 m/s?

½ × 5 × 16

Answer: 40 J

Example

10 kg raised 5 m (g = 10)?

10 × 10 × 5

Answer: 500 J

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square the speed in KE.
  • Saying holding a heavy bag still does work on it.
  • Using minutes instead of seconds when finding power.

faq.q: Does a person carrying a load on a level road do work against gravity?
faq.a: No, the force of gravity is at right angles to the motion, so no work is done against it.

faq.q: What happens to KE when the speed is doubled?
faq.a: It becomes four times, because KE depends on v².
